subject.title: fix(gateway): reap stale MCP processes on session reset regardless of…

question: Which lifecycle contract should gate MCP runtime retirement during reset/delete timeouts?
rationale: The stale-process bug needs a fix, but immediate pre-drain disposal can break active MCP work; choosing force-clear semantics versus lease-deferred retirement is maintainer lifecycle policy, not a safe mechanical edit.

options.title: Repair lifecycle contract first
options.body: Require retirement only after drain, explicit force-clear, or lease-aware deferred disposal, with reset/delete timeout tests before merge.

options.title: Accept immediate-disposal risk
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept that reset/delete may close MCP transports under a still-active old run, but that should be an explicit availability tradeoff.

options.title: Pause for broader MCP runtime repair
options.body: Pause or close this branch if the intended fix is the broader atomic lease/deferred-retirement runtime design.

recommendation.title: Repair lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Require retirement only after drain, explicit force-clear, or lease-aware deferred disposal, with reset/delete timeout tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the current assignee and provided the most specific related lifecycle-safety decision on the closed rebind PR.
